claims.text: FR's voltage drop per amp of pack current is about 3.2× that of the other inverters in all 3 snapshots, so the anomaly is consistent and specific to the FR branch.

At an equal current share FR's branch resistance would be 26.1 mΩ against 8.3 mΩ for the others. Over the 21%–29% share allowed it would be 21.9–32.0 mΩ, so extra resistance in the FR branch fits the data.

The engineers found a blackened terminal and measured high contact resistance on the bench. This is a reported finding that agrees with the extra-branch-resistance reading, but it was not recorded in the electrical data. It does not by itself show that this terminal caused the whole FR drop.

The electrical data alone cannot separate a contact fault from a conductor fault, because both add branch resistance. The bench observation of a blackened terminal favours the contact, but the conductor stays open on the data alone.
An FR sensor gain error is weakened, because it would also show about -4.78 V at rest, while FR reads +0.01 V from the others at rest. It is not excluded, since an offset could partly cancel it.
No post-repair data is given, so it is not yet known whether re-crimping removed the FR slope. A snapshot taken after the repair is needed to confirm.
The temperature dependence of pack resistance cannot be attributed to temperature alone, because state of charge and launch length also differ.
